definitions.en: About KOA · ဘၣ်ဃး KOA
Born from collaboration among Karen leaders across the United States, KOA advocates, educates, connects, and stands in solidarity.
In 2018, leaders recognized that communities in many places could act with greater strength together.
KOUSA and KAO leaders began discussing deeper collaboration and national unity.
More than fifty leaders representing twenty states met to build a common direction.
KOA connects local strength to national advocacy, language access, and collective care.
United and empowered in the United States, with the confidence and resources to shape their own future and advocate for justice in Burma.
Karen Organization of America was established in August 2018 to advocate for, promote, and advance the wellbeing of Karen people in the United States.
Meet the people KOAmerica has introduced to its community.
KOA's first public digital annual report will bring program outcomes, partnerships, and financial stewardship into one accessible view.

A protected shell for source-led translation proposals and human review.
S'gaw-Mango AI · ကညီကျိာ်တၢ်ပညိၣ်
A Karen language tool, built by the Karen community. Dictionary, translation, glyph recognition, and sentence construction — every word reviewed, every voice belonging to someone.
From syllables on paper to syllables in the air.
S'gaw-Mango AI connects community-reviewed language tools into one pipeline. Every capability traces to a real evidence artifact and a real reviewer.
Every word is reviewed. Every voice belongs to someone.
S'gaw-Mango AI does not learn from scraped text or unreviewed submissions. Every training datum traces to one approved translation proposal whose reviewer is a real human contributor.
The language grows because people give to it.
Every correction, recording, and sentence pair helps the next generation of Karen speakers. Contributions pass through the Language Studio before they become training data.

definitions.en: S'gaw Karen is monosyllabic and tonal — one syllable, one tone, one meaning. These rules are documented by the people who speak the language, reviewed by community verifiers.
Every rule here passed review. Each links the sentences that show it at work.
See a rule inside a sentence.
Paste a Karen sentence. Highlighted spans show the grammar rule that governs them — hover or tap to reveal. Annotations are made by members and agents, then verified.
You know a rule. Write it down.

Karen Music Director · တၢ်မၤစၢၤကညီဂီတ
Preserve Karen hymns, equip music directors with a bilingual editor, and connect the Karen music tradition to the language stack. The sound of home, carried forward.
A bilingual tool for Karen music directors.
The chord-chart editor supports Karen typing mode, chord placement above lyric lines, and print-ready PDF export. Use it to preserve existing hymns or compose new arrangements.
This is a live preview of the bilingual chord-chart editor. It runs as a separate service on the KOA platform. For production, the editor will be available at
Karen Music Director — chord-chart editor preview
The editor requires the local Karen Music Director service running on port 4177. If the frame above is blank, start the service or visit the editor directly. This embed uses
from the integration spec; production will use a subdomain with reverse proxy.

Karen hymns follow established patterns — predominantly 4/4 meter, verse–chorus form, I–IV–V–I harmony with stepwise melody within an octave. Lyrics use S'gaw Karen script with English chord symbols above the line.
Stepwise melody with characteristic descending cadences
Karen-script lyrics with English chord notation
Every hymn, chart, and recording helps preserve the Karen music tradition for the next generation. All contributions pass through a rights review before publication.
Photograph or scan a handwritten chord chart. Our OCR will extract the content for music-director review.
Record a Karen hymn or song. Every recording requires speaker consent and passes through a rights review.
Found an error in a published hymn's lyrics? Your correction enters the Language Studio as a translation proposal.

definitions.en: Karen sounds different in Mae La than in Hpa-An, in a camp than in a city. When you verify a word, your geography travels with it — so future speakers know whose Karen approved it.
Verifiers are community members who check dictionary entries, grammar rules, and translations before they are published to the public lexicon.
Check headwords, definitions, and translations against your own knowledge. Approve, request changes, or reject with a note.

Karen hymns follow established patterns — predominantly 4/4 meter, verse–chorus form, I–IV–V–I harmony with stepwise melody within an octave. Lyrics use S'gaw Karen script with English chord symbols above the line.
